name: MonarchTabularNumberStyle
title: TabularNumber
wrapsNative: Text with .monospacedDigit(), numbers formatted by a FormatStyle (.number, .percent, .currency(code:))
summary: Fixed-width digits for text, so that columns of figures line up and changing values do not jitter: a modifier for text that is already formatted, and a Text initialiser that formats a number or shows a dash when there is none.
whenToUse: For figures in tables and lists, totals, counters and timers. Use Text(monarchTabular:format:) for a number that may be missing and monarchTabularNumber() for text that is already formatted or that counts by itself.
whenNotToUse: Not for numbers inside a sentence, where proportional digits read better. For a number that is never missing, Text(value, format:) with monospacedDigit() is the same thing.
api: Text.init<F: FormatStyle>(monarchTabular value: F.FormatInput?, format: F, emptyText: String? = nil, emptyLabel: String? = nil) where F.FormatOutput == String

options.name: value
options.description: The number, or nil when there is none. A floating-point number that is not finite counts as missing.

options.name: format
options.description: How the number is written: .number, .percent, .currency(code:) and their options. It uses the user's locale unless it names one.

options.name: emptyText
options.description: Shown in place of a missing number. Built in: an em dash.

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Read by VoiceOver in place of a missing number. Built in: "No value".

states.name: value
states.description: The formatted number in fixed-width digits.

states.name: missing
states.description: The value is nil or not finite: an em dash is shown and VoiceOver reads "No value".

appearance: Only the digit widths change. Size, weight and colour come from the type role and the foreground style applied to the text, in every theme. The dash for a missing value takes the colour of the text around it; the web draws it in the subtle text colour, which is foregroundStyle(theme.colors.textSubtle).
platformNotes: The web TabularNumber formats with Intl.NumberFormat; iOS uses the FormatStyle passed in, so every option of the platform is available and nothing is re-implemented. The modifier is the system monospacedDigit() under a Monarch name. The web never breaks a line inside a number; on iOS a number that does not fit wraps, and lineLimit(1) or fixedSize() is the app's choice. Android covers this with a text style in MonarchTypography.
accessibility: A formatted number is read by VoiceOver as its text.
A missing value is read as "No value" (or emptyLabel), not as a dash.
The text scales with Dynamic Type through the type role applied to it.
Number formatting follows the user's locale, including digits, grouping and decimal separators.
edgeCases: NaN and infinity are shown as missing, like nil.
Only digits get one width. Separators, signs and currency symbols keep their own widths, so align columns to the trailing edge.
A custom font family without fixed-width digits is not changed by the style.
The Text initialiser returns a Text, so it can be placed inside other text by interpolation; the VoiceOver label of the dash then applies to that fragment.
